decisions.choice: true: valid as evidence, able to stand in a court
alternatives: true as opposed to false, as if Jesus were admitting that he lies
decisions.reason: Jesus speaks in the terms of a court. The law of Moses lets a charge stand only on the evidence of two or three witnesses (Deuteronomy 19:15; compare 17:6; Numbers 35:30), so a person's word about himself, standing alone, does not settle a case. Jesus grants the rule and goes on to name the witnesses who stand with him. In 8:13-14 his opponents turn the rule against him, and he answers that his testimony is true even about himself, because he knows where he came from; there "true" means truthful, and he again names the Father as the second witness (8:17-18). The two sayings do not conflict: one is about what counts as evidence, the other about whether he speaks the truth.

decisions.choice: testify, testimony: the language of a trial, which runs through the rest of the chapter
decisions.reason: Jesus answers the charges of 5:16-18 as if in court, calling his witnesses one by one: John (5:33-35), the works the Father gave him (5:36), the Father himself (5:37) and the Scriptures (5:39); then he names Moses as the one who accuses his hearers (5:45). The verb and the noun for testifying occur eleven times in 5:31-39.
The same pair of words for the verb and the noun throughout 5:31-39, as in 1:7 and 3:11, so the reader can follow the chain of witnesses. Readable uses "witness" only for the person who testifies.
In a court, someone who testifies about himself speaks for his own case; Balanced says so plainly (meaning decision m1).

decisions.choice: the only witness ... does not count as true
alternatives: If I testify about myself, my testimony is not true
decisions.reason: Readable spells out the legal point (meaning decision m1), so that Jesus does not sound as if he were admitting to lying.
The same pair of words for the verb and the noun throughout 5:31-39, as in 1:7 and 3:11, so the reader can follow the chain of witnesses (meaning decision m2).

decisions.choice: el único que habla a mi favor ... no se podría tomar como verdadero
decisions.reason: As in English: Readable spells out the legal point (meaning decision m1), so Jesus does not sound as if he were admitting to lying. Every plural "you" in this passage is the ustedes / vosotros reader setting.

decisions.choice: rendre témoignage, le témoignage at every level; témoin (R) for the person
decisions.reason: The book-wide French choice for John, recorded once in this passage: one pair of words for the verb and the noun throughout 5:31-39, so the reader can follow the chain of witnesses in what is the language of a trial (meaning decision m2). Readable keeps them too, since the English Readable does, and uses "témoin" only for the person who testifies.

decisions.choice: ne peut pas être tenu pour vrai (R)
decisions.reason: As in English, Readable says that such testimony does not count as evidence (meaning decision m1), so that Jesus does not sound as if he were admitting to lying; "tenir pour vrai" is the plain French for accepting something as true.

decisions.choice: No deity_pronoun spans; Jesus's "나" and the Father's "그분" stay as they are
alternatives: capitalised pronoun spans as in English
decisions.reason: Korean has no capital letters, so the reader setting has nothing to change. Respect for God and Jesus is carried by the honorific "-시-", "께서" and "그분" at every level. This holds for the whole passage.

decisions.choice: Jesus speaks in the plain style (해라체: "참되지 않다", "생각하지 마라", "믿겠느냐") through the whole speech
decisions.reason: The style guide sets 해라체 for Jesus speaking to crowds and opponents; the Father, spoken of inside the speech, still takes the subject honorific (아버지께서 보내셨다). This holds for the whole passage.

decisions.choice: "Ta" for Jesus; "các người" for the hearers
decisions.reason: Jesus is still speaking to the Jewish leaders who oppose him (5:16-18). As the style guide sets for the book, he speaks of himself as "Ta" and addresses opponents as "các người", throughout this passage.

decisions.choice: testemunhar ... o testemunho at every level
decisions.reason: As the English: one pair of words for the verb and the noun through 5:31-39, the language of a court (meaning decision m2), so the reader can follow the chain of witnesses. Readable uses "testemunha" only for the person who testifies.

decisions.choice: no deity_pronoun spans in Amharic: pronouns for Jesus and the Father are written plainly (ስለ ራሴ, ምስክርነቴ)
decisions.reason: The Ethiopic script has no capital letters, so the reader's setting for capitalised pronouns has nothing to change in Amharic. Pronouns for God and for Jesus are written plainly throughout this passage.

decisions.choice: መመስከር (testify) and ምስክርነት (testimony) at every level, through 5:31-39
decisions.reason: The language of a trial runs through this passage (meaning decision m2), so the verb and the noun stay the same Amharic words at every level. "ምስክርነት" is the testimony given; "ምስክር" is the person who gives it.

alternatives: a deity_pronoun span as in the English
decisions.reason: Devanagari has no capital letters, so the setting has nothing to change. Respect for Jesus and the Father is carried by honorific forms ("पिता ... देते हैं", "उनकी") at every level. This applies to the whole passage.

One Hindi pair for the verb and the noun throughout 5:31-39, so the reader can follow the chain of witnesses. "सच्ची" means valid as evidence (meaning decision m1); Readable spells out the legal point.
The same pair of words for the verb and the noun throughout 5:31-39, so the reader can follow the chain of witnesses in what is the language of a trial (meaning decision m2).

Truth is a key term: "истина" at Literal and Balanced, "правда" at Readable (style guide, section 6). Readable adds "не считается" so that Jesus does not sound as if he were admitting to lying (meaning decision m1).

The language of a trial runs through verses 31-39 (meaning decision m2), so the same verb and noun are kept throughout. Of testimony, "правдивий" says that it holds as evidence (meaning decision m1); "істина" is kept for the noun truth.

decisions.choice: "証しする" and "証し" at every level
decisions.reason: The same pair of words for the verb and the noun through 5:31-39, so that the reader can follow the chain of witnesses (meaning decision m2); "証し" is the book's word for testimony, and "証言" is kept for a witness in court (18:23).

decisions.choice: "真実とは認められない" (B); "本当のこととは認められない" (R)
decisions.reason: "True" here means valid as evidence (meaning decision m1): "認められない" says that a court would not accept it, so that Jesus does not sound as if he admitted to lying. Literal keeps "真実ではない".

decisions.reason: John is named in the next verse, and some have taken him to be the other witness. But Jesus goes on to say that he does not accept testimony from a human being (5:34), that he has testimony greater than John's (5:36), and that the Father who sent him has testified about him (5:37). In 8:18 he says it outright: the Father who sent him testifies about him. The present tense "testifies" and Jesus's "I know" fit the Father best.

decisions.choice: the second witness the law requires
decisions.reason: With the Father beside him, Jesus is not a lone witness, and the rule of two witnesses (Deuteronomy 19:15) is met, as he says again in 8:17-18.

As in English: Readable names the other witness (meaning decision m1).

alternatives: de moi, à mon sujet, with no setting
decisions.reason: Where Jesus speaks of himself French often needs the stressed pronoun "moi" or a possessive ("à mon sujet") where English has "me"; these take the deity_pronoun setting like the English pronouns. "Je" has none, as the brief directs. This applies throughout the passage.
Korean must decide whether to honour the other witness. The meaning decision identifies him as the Father, so every level uses the honorific; this hints at who is meant before Readable names him.

Vietnamese must choose a classifier for "another". "Đấng" is used for a revered person, God or Jesus, and the other witness is the Father (meaning decision). The same "Đấng" is used for "the one who sent me" through the passage.

decisions.choice: honorific "वे ... देते हैं" for the other witness
decisions.reason: The other witness is the Father (meaning decision m1), and God spoken of takes honorific forms; Hindi grammar therefore hints at who is meant even where only Readable names him.

decisions.choice: "おられる", "なさる" (B, R) for the other witness
decisions.reason: The other witness is the Father (meaning decision m1), so Balanced and Readable already speak of him with the light respect form Jesus uses for God; Literal keeps the neutral "方" and leaves him unnamed, as the Greek does.

source.text: ὑμεῖς ἀπεστάλκατε πρὸς Ἰωάννην, καὶ μεμαρτύρηκε τῇ ἀληθείᾳ·

records.literal_gloss: You have sent to John, and he has testified to the truth;

en.L: You yourselves have sent [messengers] to John, and he has testified to the truth.
en.B: You yourselves sent messengers to John, and he has testified to the truth.
en.R: You sent messengers to ask John questions, and he testified to the truth.

es.L: {{plural_you:Ustedes han enviado|Vosotros habéis enviado}} [mensajeros] a Juan, y él ha dado testimonio de la verdad.
es.B: {{plural_you:Ustedes mismos enviaron|Vosotros mismos enviasteis}} mensajeros a Juan, y él ha dado testimonio de la verdad.
es.R: {{plural_you:Ustedes enviaron|Vosotros enviasteis}} mensajeros a hacerle preguntas a Juan, y él dio testimonio de la verdad.

fr.L: Vous, vous avez envoyé [des messagers] auprès de Jean, et il a rendu témoignage à la vérité.
fr.B: Vous-mêmes, vous avez envoyé des messagers à Jean, et il a rendu témoignage à la vérité.
fr.R: Vous avez envoyé des messagers poser des questions à Jean, et il a rendu témoignage à la vérité.

sw.L: Ninyi mmetuma [wajumbe] kwa Yohana, naye ametoa ushuhuda kwa ile kweli.
sw.B: Ninyi wenyewe mlipeleka wajumbe kwa Yohana, naye ametoa ushuhuda kwa ajili ya kweli.
sw.R: Mlituma wajumbe kumwuliza Yohana maswali, naye akaishuhudia kweli.

vi.L: Chính các người đã sai [người] đến cùng Giăng, và ông ấy đã làm chứng cho chân lý.
vi.B: Chính các người đã sai người đến gặp Giăng, và ông ấy đã làm chứng cho chân lý.
vi.R: Các người đã sai người đến hỏi Giăng nhiều điều, và ông ấy đã làm chứng cho chân lý.

ko.L: 너희가 요한에게 [사람들을] 보냈고, 그는 진리에 대하여 증언하였다.
ko.B: 너희는 요한에게 사람들을 보냈고, 요한은 진리에 대하여 증언했다.
ko.R: 너희는 요한에게 사람들을 보내서 물어보았고, 요한은 진리에 대해 증언했다.

pt.L: Vocês mesmos enviaram [mensageiros] a João, e ele tem dado testemunho da verdade.
pt.B: Vocês mesmos enviaram mensageiros a João, e ele deu testemunho da verdade.
pt.R: Vocês enviaram mensageiros para fazer perguntas a João, e ele deu testemunho da verdade.

am.L: እናንተ ራሳችሁ ወደ ዮሐንስ [መልእክተኞችን] ልካችኋል፤ እርሱም ለእውነት መስክሯል።
am.B: እናንተ ራሳችሁ ወደ ዮሐንስ መልእክተኞችን ላካችሁ፤ እርሱም ለእውነት መስክሯል።
am.R: እናንተ ዮሐንስን እንዲጠይቁ መልእክተኞችን ላካችሁ፤ እርሱም ስለ እውነት መሰከረ።

hi.L: तुमने ही यूहन्ना के पास [दूत] भेजे हैं, और उसने सत्य की गवाही दी है।
hi.B: तुमने ख़ुद यूहन्ना के पास दूत भेजे, और उसने सत्य की गवाही दी है।
hi.R: तुमने यूहन्ना से सवाल पूछने के लिए लोग भेजे थे, और उसने सच की गवाही दी।

ru.L: Вы сами послали [людей] к Иоанну, и он засвидетельствовал истину.
ru.B: Вы сами посылали людей к Иоанну, и он засвидетельствовал истину.
ru.R: Вы посылали людей расспросить Иоанна, и он засвидетельствовал правду.

uk.L: Ви самі послали [посланців] до Івана, і він засвідчив істину.
uk.B: Ви самі посилали посланців до Івана, і він засвідчив істину.
uk.R: Ви посилали людей розпитати Івана, і він засвідчив правду.

ja.L: あなたがたは、ヨハネのもとに[人々を]遣わした。そして彼は、真理について証しした。
ja.B: あなたがた自身が、ヨハネのもとに使いを送った。そして彼は真理について証ししたのである。
ja.R: あなたたちは、ヨハネに質問するために使いを送った。そしてヨハネは、本当のことを証しした。

decisions.choice: the delegation sent from Jerusalem to question John (1:19-28)
decisions.reason: The Jewish authorities in Jerusalem sent priests and Levites to ask John who he was (1:19, 24). He told them he was not the Christ and pointed to the one coming after him (1:20, 26-27); the next day he called Jesus the Lamb of God (1:29). Jesus is speaking to the same authorities (5:16-18), and the pronoun "you" is emphatic: you yourselves asked for John's testimony.

decisions.choice: the truth: the truth about who Jesus is
decisions.reason: John's testimony was about Jesus (1:15, 29-34). The perfect tense "has testified" means that his testimony still stands, though John's own work is over (5:35).

decisions.choice: [messengers] (L); messengers (B); messengers to ask John questions (R)
decisions.reason: The Greek leaves the object of "sent" unstated; each level says who was sent (meaning decision m1), Literal in brackets.
Shows the emphatic pronoun (meaning decision m1).
As in English: the Greek leaves the object of "sent" unstated (meaning decision m1). "Él" here is John and has no setting.

"Testemunhar a verdade" with a direct object would mean "witnessed (saw) the truth"; "dar testemunho da verdade" says that John spoke for it. Literal "tem dado" keeps the perfect, whose testimony still stands (meaning decision m2).
Shows the emphatic pronoun: they themselves had sent to John (1:19-28).
The truth about who Jesus is (meaning decision m2). "真理" is the key term; Readable says "本当のこと" for what is true, as the brief allows.

source.text: ἐγὼ δὲ οὐ παρὰ ἀνθρώπου τὴν μαρτυρίαν λαμβάνω, ἀλλὰ ταῦτα λέγω ἵνα ὑμεῖς σωθῆτε.

records.literal_gloss: But I not from a human the testimony receive, but these things I say so that you may be saved.

en.L: But I do not receive [my] testimony from {{gender:a human being|man}}; rather, I say these things so that you may be saved.
en.B: Yet I do not accept testimony from {{gender:a human being|man}}; I say these things so that you may be saved.
en.R: I do not depend on testimony from {{gender:people|men}}. I am telling you about John so that you can be saved.

es.L: Pero yo no recibo [{{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}}] testimonio de {{gender:un ser humano|hombre}}, sino que digo estas cosas para que {{plural_you:ustedes sean salvos|vosotros seáis salvos}}.
es.B: Pero yo no acepto el testimonio de {{gender:ningún ser humano|ningún hombre}}; digo estas cosas para que {{plural_you:ustedes sean salvos|vosotros seáis salvos}}.
es.R: Yo no dependo del testimonio de {{gender:la gente|los hombres}}. {{plural_you:Les|Os}} hablo de Juan para que {{plural_you:ustedes puedan|vosotros podáis}} ser salvos.

fr.L: Mais je ne reçois pas [mon] témoignage d’{{gender:un être humain|un homme}} ; je dis plutôt ces choses afin que vous soyez sauvés.
fr.B: Je n’accepte pourtant pas le témoignage d’{{gender:un être humain|un homme}} ; je dis cela pour que vous soyez sauvés.
fr.R: Je ne compte pas sur le témoignage {{gender:des gens|des hommes}}. Si je vous parle de Jean, c’est pour que vous soyez sauvés.

sw.L: Lakini {{deity_pronoun:mimi|Mimi}} sipokei ushuhuda kutoka kwa mwanadamu; badala yake ninasema mambo haya ili ninyi mwokolewe.
sw.B: Lakini sipokei ushuhuda kutoka kwa mwanadamu; nasema haya ili mpate kuokolewa.
sw.R: Sitegemei ushuhuda wa watu. Nawaambia habari za Yohana ili mpate kuokolewa.

vi.L: Nhưng {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} không nhận lời chứng từ loài người; trái lại, {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} nói những điều này để các người được cứu.
vi.B: Tuy vậy, {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} không cần lời chứng của loài người; {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} nói những điều này là để các người được cứu.
vi.R: Ta không cần người ta làm chứng cho {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}. Ta nhắc đến Giăng là để các người có thể được cứu.

ko.L: 그러나 나는 사람에게서 증언을 받지 않는다. 다만 너희가 구원을 받게 하려고 이것들을 말한다.
ko.B: 나는 사람의 증언을 받아들이지 않는다. 내가 이런 말을 하는 것은 너희가 구원을 받게 하려는 것이다.
ko.R: 나는 사람들의 증언에 기대지 않는다. 내가 요한 이야기를 하는 것은 너희가 구원을 받게 하려는 것이다.

pt.L: Mas eu não recebo o [meu] testemunho de {{gender:um ser humano|homem}}; antes, digo estas coisas para que vocês sejam salvos.
pt.B: Mas eu não aceito testemunho de {{gender:um ser humano|homem}}; digo estas coisas para que vocês sejam salvos.
pt.R: Eu não dependo do testemunho {{gender:das pessoas|dos homens}}. Estou falando de João para que vocês possam ser salvos.

am.L: እኔ ግን ከሰው ምስክርነትን አልቀበልም፤ ነገር ግን እናንተ እንድትድኑ ይህን እላለሁ።
am.B: እኔ ግን ከሰው ምስክርነት አልቀበልም፤ ይህን የምለው እናንተ እንድትድኑ ነው።
am.R: እኔ በሰዎች ምስክርነት አልተማመንም። ስለ ዮሐንስ የምነግራችሁ እናንተ እንድትድኑ ነው።

hi.L: पर मैं मनुष्य से [अपनी] गवाही नहीं लेता; बल्कि मैं ये बातें इसलिए कहता हूँ कि तुम उद्धार पाओ।
hi.B: फिर भी मैं मनुष्य की गवाही स्वीकार नहीं करता; मैं ये बातें इसलिए कहता हूँ कि तुम्हारा उद्धार हो।
hi.R: मैं लोगों की गवाही पर निर्भर नहीं हूँ। मैं तुम्हें यूहन्ना के बारे में इसलिए बता रहा हूँ ताकि तुम्हारा उद्धार हो सके।

ru.L: Но {{deity_pronoun:я|Я}} принимаю свидетельство не от человека; это же говорю, чтобы вы были спасены.
ru.B: Впрочем, {{deity_pronoun:я|Я}} не принимаю свидетельства от человека; {{deity_pronoun:я|Я}} говорю это, чтобы вы были спасены.
ru.R: Мне не нужно свидетельство от людей. Я говорю вам об Иоанне, чтобы вы могли спастись.

uk.L: Але {{deity_pronoun:я|Я}} не від людини приймаю [своє] свідчення, а кажу це, щоб ви спаслися.
uk.B: Проте {{deity_pronoun:я|Я}} не приймаю свідчення від людини; кажу це, щоб ви були спасенні.
uk.R: Мені не потрібне свідчення від людей. Я розповідаю вам про Івана, щоб ви могли бути врятовані.

ja.L: しかし、わたしは人から証しを受けるのではない。むしろ、あなたがたが救われるために、これらのことを言うのである。
ja.B: わたしは、人からの証しを受け入れるのではない。わたしがこれらのことを言うのは、あなたがたが救われるためである。
ja.R: わたしは、人の証しに頼ってはいない。わたしがヨハネのことを話すのは、あなたたちが救われるためだ。

decisions.choice: Jesus does not depend on human testimony; he mentions John for his hearers' sake
alternatives: Jesus rejects John's testimony as false
decisions.reason: John's testimony was true (5:33), but Jesus's claim does not rest on any human witness; the one who vouches for him is the Father (5:32, 37). The article ("the testimony") points to the testimony that counts for him. He reminds his hearers of John because they once welcomed John (5:35), and John's word could still lead them to him.

decisions.choice: be saved: rescued from judgment and given life
decisions.reason: As in 3:17, and in the terms of this chapter: the one who hears Jesus's word and believes the one who sent him has eternal life and does not come into judgment (5:24).
The Greek article points to the testimony Jesus relies on (meaning decision m1); Literal supplies "my" in brackets.

The verb means receive or accept. It recurs through the passage: Jesus does not accept glory from people (5:41), they do not accept him (5:43), and they accept glory from one another (5:44). Balanced says "accept" each time and Literal "receive" each time, so the thread stays visible.
"These things" refers to what Jesus has just said about John's testimony; Readable says so.

decisions.choice: a human being (L, B); people (R), under the gender setting
decisions.reason: The word means any human being, not a male; the traditional "man" is the alternative, as in 2:25.

decisions.choice: {{gender:un ser humano|hombre}} (L); {{gender:ningún ser humano|ningún hombre}} (B); {{gender:la gente|los hombres}} (R)
decisions.reason: The word means any human being, not a male (meaning decision m1); inclusive default, traditional one tap away.
As in English: "estas cosas" refers to what Jesus has just said about John.

The verb returns in 5:41, 5:43 and 5:44, where Jesus does not accept glory from people, they do not accept him, and they accept glory from one another. As in English, Literal says "recevoir" and Balanced "accepter" each time, so the thread stays visible; Readable says "compter sur" here, where the sense is relying on a witness, and "accepter" after.

decisions.choice: d’{{gender:un être humain|un homme}} (L, B); {{gender:des gens|des hommes}} (R)
decisions.reason: The word means any human being (meaning decision m1 and the English decision), so the inclusive word is the default and the traditional "homme" the alternative; both begin with a vowel, so the elided "d’" stays outside the span.

alternatives: a gender setting span as in English
decisions.reason: Korean "사람" already means a human being of either sex, so there is nothing for the gender setting to change; the same holds for "사람들" in 5:41. This holds for the whole passage.

decisions.choice: "loài người" (L, B); "người ta" (R), with no gender span
decisions.reason: Vietnamese "loài người" and "người ta" already include men and women, so there is no second wording for a gender setting to offer. This holds for "loài người" in 5:41 too.

decisions.choice: ሰው (a human being, L, B); ሰዎች (people, R), with no gender span
alternatives: a span like the English {{gender:a human being|man}}
decisions.reason: "ሰው" and "ሰዎች" already mean human beings of either sex, so Amharic has no second wording for the setting to switch to; this holds for the passage (verse 41).
The English has a gender span here and in 5:41. "मनुष्य" and "लोग" already mean human beings of either sex, so Hindi needs no span.

decisions.choice: "человека" (L, B); "людей" (R), with no gender span; also "от людей" in 5:41
decisions.reason: The English has a gender span here. Russian "человек" and "люди" already mean human beings of either sex (meaning: any human being), so no setting is needed.
The English Literal supplies "my" for the Greek article; Russian has no article, and the word order already puts the weight on "не от человека".

decisions.choice: "від людини" (L, B), "від людей" (R), with no gender setting, here and in verse 41
decisions.reason: The English offers "man" as the traditional alternative; the Ukrainian words "людина" and "люди" are both the traditional and the inclusive ones, so no setting is needed.
The English has a gender span (a human being/man, people/men); Japanese "人" already means any human being, so no span is needed. The same holds for "人々" in 5:41.
The verb "receive, accept" recurs through 5:41-44; Literal and Balanced keep "受ける / 受け入れる" there too, so the thread stays visible.

source.text: ἐκεῖνος ἦν ὁ λύχνος ὁ καιόμενος καὶ φαίνων, ὑμεῖς δὲ ἠθελήσατε ἀγαλλιαθῆναι πρὸς ὥραν ἐν τῷ φωτὶ αὐτοῦ·

records.literal_gloss: That one was the lamp the [one] burning and shining, and you were willing to rejoice for an hour in the light of him;

en.L: That one was the lamp that was burning and shining, and you were willing for a while to rejoice in his light.
en.B: John was the lamp that burned and shone, and for a little while you were glad to rejoice in his light.
en.R: John was like a lamp that was lit and shining. For a short time you were happy to enjoy his light.

es.L: Aquel era la lámpara que ardía y alumbraba, y {{plural_you:ustedes quisieron regocijarse|vosotros quisisteis regocijaros}} por un tiempo en su luz.
es.B: Juan era la lámpara que ardía y alumbraba, y por un poco de tiempo {{plural_you:ustedes quisieron alegrarse|vosotros quisisteis alegraros}} con su luz.
es.R: Juan era como una lámpara encendida que alumbraba. Por un tiempo {{plural_you:ustedes estuvieron|vosotros estuvisteis}} contentos de disfrutar de su luz.

fr.L: Celui-là était la lampe qui brûlait et brillait, et vous, vous avez bien voulu, pour un temps, vous réjouir à sa lumière.
fr.B: Jean était la lampe qui brûlait et éclairait, et vous avez bien voulu, un court moment, vous réjouir à sa lumière.
fr.R: Jean était comme une lampe allumée qui brillait. Pendant un peu de temps, vous avez été contents de profiter de sa lumière.

sw.L: Yule alikuwa ndiye taa inayowaka na kumulika, nanyi mlikuwa tayari kwa kitambo kushangilia katika nuru yake.
sw.B: Yohana alikuwa taa iliyowaka na kung'aa, na kwa muda mfupi mlifurahi kushangilia katika nuru yake.
sw.R: Yohana alikuwa kama taa iliyowashwa na kung'aa. Kwa muda mfupi mlifurahi kufaidi nuru yake.

vi.L: Ông ấy là ngọn đèn đang cháy và chiếu sáng, còn các người thì đã muốn vui mừng một lúc trong ánh sáng của ông ấy.
vi.B: Giăng là ngọn đèn cháy và chiếu sáng, và trong một thời gian ngắn các người đã vui lòng hớn hở trong ánh sáng của ông ấy.
vi.R: Giăng giống như một ngọn đèn được thắp lên và chiếu sáng. Trong một thời gian ngắn, các người đã vui thích ánh sáng của ông ấy.

ko.L: 그는 타오르며 빛을 비추는 등불이었고, 너희는 잠시 동안 그의 빛 안에서 즐거워하기를 원하였다.
ko.B: 요한은 타오르며 빛나는 등불이었다. 너희는 잠시 동안 그 빛 속에서 기꺼이 즐거워했다.
ko.R: 요한은 불이 켜져서 환하게 비추는 등불과 같았다. 너희는 잠깐 동안 그 빛을 좋아하며 즐거워했다.

pt.L: Aquele era a candeia que ardia e brilhava, e vocês quiseram se alegrar por um tempo na luz dele.
pt.B: João era a candeia que ardia e brilhava, e por pouco tempo vocês tiveram prazer em se alegrar com a luz dele.
pt.R: João era como uma lamparina acesa e brilhando. Por pouco tempo vocês ficaram felizes com a luz dele.

decisions.reason: John was not the light but came to testify about the light (1:8); Jesus is the light (1:9; 8:12). A lamp shines, but it has to be lit, and it burns down. The article may point to a familiar picture: in Psalm 132:17 God says he has prepared a lamp for his anointed one.
The past tense speaks of John's witness as finished. By this time he may have been put in prison or put to death; 3:24 notes that at an earlier point he had not yet been imprisoned.

The Greek has only "that one"; Balanced and Readable name John, so that no reader takes it to be Jesus.

records.literal_gloss: But I have the testimony greater than of John; for the works which has given to me the Father so that I may complete them, the very works which I do, testify about me that the Father me has sent. \v 37 And the having-sent me Father, that one has testified about me.

en.L: But I have the testimony greater than John's; for the works that the Father has given {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} so that I may complete them, the very works that I do, testify about {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} that the Father has sent {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}. \v 37 And the Father who sent {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} has testified about {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}.
en.B: But I have a testimony greater than John's. The works the Father has given {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} to bring to completion, the works themselves that I am doing, testify about {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}: they show that the Father has sent {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}. \v 37 And the Father who sent {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} has testified about {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} {{deity_pronoun:himself|Himself}}.
en.R: But I have testimony that is greater than John's. The Father has given {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} works to do and to finish. These works that I am doing testify about {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}. They show that the Father has sent {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}. \v 37 And the Father who sent {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} has {{deity_pronoun:himself|Himself}} testified about {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}.

es.B: Pero yo tengo un testimonio mayor que el de Juan. Las obras que el Padre {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} ha encargado llevar a término, las mismas obras que estoy haciendo, dan testimonio de {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}}: muestran que el Padre {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} ha enviado. \v 37 Y el Padre que {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} envió ha dado testimonio de {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}} {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} mismo.
es.R: Pero yo tengo un testimonio más grande que el de Juan. El Padre {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} ha dado obras para hacer y terminar. Estas obras que estoy haciendo dan testimonio de {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}}. Muestran que el Padre {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} ha enviado. \v 37 Y el Padre que {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} envió ha dado testimonio de {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}} {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} mismo.

Elles montrent que le Père {{deity_pronoun:m’|M’}}a envoyé. \v 37 Et le Père qui {{deity_pronoun:m’|M’}}a envoyé a {{deity_pronoun:lui-même|Lui-même}} rendu témoignage à {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} sujet.

sw.R: Lakini {{deity_pronoun:mimi|Mimi}} nina ushuhuda mkuu kuliko wa Yohana. Baba amenipa kazi za kufanya na kuzimaliza. Kazi hizi ninazozifanya zinanishuhudia. ko.B: 그러나 나에게는 요한의 증언보다 더 큰 증언이 있다. 아버지께서 나에게 맡기셔서 끝까지 이루게 하신 일들, 곧 내가 지금 하고 있는 바로 그 일들이 나에 대하여 증언한다. 그 일들은 아버지께서 나를 보내셨다는 것을 보여 준다. \v 37 그리고 나를 보내신 아버지께서 친히 나에 대하여 증언하셨다.

pt.R: Mas eu tenho um testemunho maior que o de João. O Pai {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} deu obras para fazer e terminar. Essas obras que estou fazendo testemunham sobre {{deity_pronoun:mim|Mim}}. decisions.choice: the works: all that the Father has given Jesus to do, his signs included
decisions.reason: Where the narrator and the crowds speak of "signs", Jesus speaks of the "works" the Father has given him (5:20; 9:3-4; 10:25, 37-38; 14:10-11). They include the healing at the pool (5:17) and the greater works of giving life and judging (5:20-22). Because the Father is at work in them, they testify that he sent Jesus.

decisions.choice: complete: carry the Father's work through to its end
decisions.reason: The same verb as in 4:34 and 17:4; from the cross Jesus says "It is finished" (19:30), a word from the same root.

decisions.choice: the Father's testimony: left open, as the text leaves it
alternatives: what God told John about the Spirit coming down on Jesus (1:33)
decisions.reason: The perfect tense says that the Father has given his testimony and that it stands. Jesus does not say how. It may be the works through which the Father acts (5:36), the Scriptures that testify about Jesus (5:39), or the sign God gave John when the Spirit came down on Jesus (1:32-34). Verse 38 adds that his hearers do not receive it, because his word does not remain in them.
The pronoun is not needed for the sense; it stresses the person: the Father himself, not a lesser witness.

decisions.choice: the works ... testify about me: they show that
alternatives: testify about me that the Father has sent me
decisions.reason: Balanced separates the testimony of the works from what it shows, so that the long Greek clause reads clearly.
Shows the emphasis of meaning decision m4.

decisions.choice: The Father has given me works to do and to finish. These works ...
decisions.reason: Readable breaks the long sentence into short ones.

decisions.choice: dan testimonio de mí: muestran que
decisions.reason: As in English: Balanced separates the testimony of the works from what it shows.

Korean cannot compare with a bare genitive; Literal supplies the noun the Greek leaves understood.
The emphatic "he" is said in Korean with an adverb of personal action; "친히" is the respectful word, "직접" the plainer one.

Portuguese shows the emphatic pronoun (meaning decision m4) with "o próprio Pai", which carries no pronoun, so the English span on "himself" has no counterpart. Literal keeps the resumed pronoun "ele".
The English has a span on "himself"; Russian "сам" takes none (style guide, section 7b). It carries the emphasis of meaning decision m4.

decisions.reason: The same verb as in 4:34, carrying the Father's work through to its end (meaning decision m2); the same Japanese is used there.
Jesus speaks of what the Father does for him with "くださる", the light respect form for God's giving; the emphatic "that one" (meaning decision m4) becomes "その方が" (L) and "ご自身が" (B, R).

decisions.choice: a contrast with Israel at Sinai
alternatives: a plain statement that no one has seen God (1:18)
decisions.reason: At Sinai Israel heard the voice of God out of the fire, though they saw no form (Deuteronomy 4:12, 15, 33), and God said that Moses sees the form of the LORD (Numbers 12:8). Jesus's hearers claim that heritage, yet they have not heard God's voice: they do not recognize it in the one he sent. The words may instead restate that no one has ever seen God except the Son (1:18; 6:46), so that the Father's testimony reaches people only through him. Both readings lead to the point of verse 38.
God's word has no lasting home in them. Jesus uses the same verb when he speaks of his words remaining in his disciples (15:7; compare 1 John 2:14).

decisions.choice: because: their unbelief shows that God's word is not in them
alternatives: their unbelief is the cause of God's word not remaining in them
decisions.reason: Unbelief here is the evidence: if God's word lived in them, they would recognize the one God sent.

John's theological "remain" (docs/john-terms.md) is "permanecer" at every level; "ficar" is kept for the ordinary sense of staying somewhere.

records.literal_gloss: You search the Scriptures, because you think in them life eternal to have; and those are the [ones] testifying about me;

en.L: You search the Scriptures, because you think you have eternal life in them; and those are the [ones] testifying about {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}.
en.B: You pore over the Scriptures, since you think that eternal life is to be found in them; and they are the ones that testify about {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}.
en.R: You study the Scriptures carefully, because you think that in them you have eternal life, the life of the age to come. And the Scriptures themselves testify about {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}.

es.B: {{plural_you:Estudian a fondo|Estudiáis a fondo}} las Escrituras, porque {{plural_you:piensan|pensáis}} que en ellas se encuentra la vida eterna; y son ellas las que dan testimonio de {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}}.
es.R: {{plural_you:Estudian|Estudiáis}} las Escrituras con cuidado, porque {{plural_you:piensan|pensáis}} que en ellas {{plural_you:tienen|tenéis}} vida eterna, la vida del mundo venidero. Y las mismas Escrituras dan testimonio de {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}}.

fr.L: Vous scrutez les Écritures, parce que vous, vous estimez avoir en elles la vie éternelle ; et ce sont elles qui rendent témoignage à {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} sujet.
fr.B: Vous étudiez de près les Écritures, car vous pensez y trouver la vie éternelle ; or ce sont elles qui rendent témoignage à {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} sujet.

Jesus goes on to give the reason they search ("because you think ...") and to say that they still will not come to him (5:40); both fit a statement about what they already do. As a command, the words would call them to search and find that the Scriptures point to him. A footnote gives the command.

decisions.choice: you think that in them you have eternal life: the Law as the way of life
decisions.reason: The Law itself promised life to those who keep it (Leviticus 18:5; Deuteronomy 30:15-20; 32:47). Jesus does not deny that the Scriptures speak of life; he says that they point to him, the one who gives it (5:21, 24-26).

decisions.choice: the Scriptures: the Jewish Scriptures, which Christians call the Old Testament
decisions.reason: The New Testament had not yet been written; Jesus means the Law, the Prophets and the other writings his hearers read.

decisions.choice: eternal life: the life of the age to come, God's own life, which begins now
decisions.reason: Key term, as in 3:15-16 and 5:24.

ru.L: Славы от людей {{deity_pronoun:я|Я}} не принимаю, \v 42 но {{deity_pronoun:я|Я}} знаю вас: любви Божьей вы в себе не имеете.

uk.L: Слави від людей {{deity_pronoun:я|Я}} не приймаю, \v 42 але {{deity_pronoun:я|Я}} пізнав вас, що любові Божої не маєте в собі.

ja.L: わたしは人々から栄光を受けない。\v 42 しかし、わたしはあなたがたを知っている。あなたがたが自分の内に神の愛を持っていないことを。
ja.B: 人々からの栄光を、わたしは受けない。\v 42 しかし、わたしはあなたがたを知っている。あなたがたの内には、神への愛がない。
ja.R: わたしは、人々からの栄光を受けようとはしない。\v 42 しかし、わたしはあなたたちのことを知っている。あなたたちは、心の中で神を愛していない。

decisions.choice: glory: honor and approval given by people
alternatives: the divine glory seen in Jesus (1:14)
decisions.reason: Here the word means the honor people give one another, a common sense of it. Jesus does not depend on human approval any more than on human testimony (5:34). The same contrast between glory from people and glory from God returns in 5:44, 7:18 and 12:43.

decisions.choice: the love of God: their love for God
alternatives: the love that comes from God
decisions.reason: The phrase can mean God's love or love for God. The context is about where their hearts are turned: they accept glory from one another and do not seek the glory that comes from God (5:44). Israel's first command was to love the LORD with all the heart (Deuteronomy 6:5), and that love is what Jesus says is missing. The other senses are close: those who have God's love in them love him in return (1 John 4:19).

decisions.choice: I know you: Jesus knows their hearts
decisions.reason: The perfect tense means a settled knowledge. As in 2:24-25, Jesus knows what is in people; here he knows these hearers and says what is missing in them.

decisions.choice: love for God (B); you do not love God (R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the phrase as it stands; Balanced and Readable give the sense chosen in meaning decision m2.

alternatives: I do not receive glory from people
decisions.reason: Literal and Balanced keep "glory" at the front, as the Greek does for emphasis.
Readable uses the everyday way of speaking about what is inside a person.

Literal keeps the phrase as it stands; Balanced and Readable give the sense chosen in meaning decision m2, their love for God.

decisions.choice: "神の愛" (L); "神への愛" (B); "神を愛していない" (R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the phrase as it stands; Balanced and Readable give the sense chosen in meaning decision m2, their love for God.
The key term is kept even where it means honor and approval from people (meaning decision m1), so that the contrast with the glory from God in 5:44 stays visible.

decisions.choice: in the name of: as his representative, with his authority
decisions.reason: To come in someone's name is to come as their envoy, carrying their authority (Deuteronomy 18:19; Psalm 118:26, which the crowd sings in 12:13). The other comes in his own name: no one has sent him.

decisions.choice: another: anyone who comes on his own authority
decisions.reason: Jesus names no one. The point is the contrast: they reject the one God sent and would welcome one whom no one sent. One who speaks on his own authority seeks his own glory (7:18), and that suits hearers who accept glory from one another (5:44).

decisions.choice: receive: welcome, accept as what he claims to be
decisions.reason: As in 1:11-12: his own did not receive him, but to all who received him he gave the right to become children of God.

decisions.choice: with my Father's authority ... on his own authority
alternatives: in my Father's name ... in his own name
decisions.reason: Readable explains the idiom (meaning decision m1).

decisions.choice: Should someone else come ..., him you will accept
alternatives: If someone else comes ..., you will accept him
decisions.reason: Balanced keeps the stress the Greek puts on "that one" at the end of the sentence.

decisions.choice: his own name, him: no gender setting
decisions.reason: The words picture a man who sets himself up against Jesus; the Greek pronoun is masculine, and the saying is kept as it stands, as with the prophet in 4:44.

decisions.choice: con la autoridad de mi Padre ... con su propia autoridad
decisions.reason: As in English: Readable explains the idiom (meaning decision m1). The "otro" is kept as it stands, with no gender setting.
The topic particle "은" gives the contrast that the English Balanced marks by putting "him" first: him you will accept, though not me.
The verb means to welcome someone and accept him as what he claims to be (meaning decision m3); Balanced and Readable use the more everyday "स्वीकार करना", as in 5:34 and 5:41.

decisions.choice: "с властью, которую дал мне мой Отец" ... "сам от себя"
decisions.reason: Readable explains the idiom "in the name of": as his representative, with his authority (meaning decision m1).

decisions.choice: "父から任されて" and "自分勝手に" (R)
decisions.reason: Readable explains the idiom "in the name of", with someone's authority (meaning decision m1); Literal and Balanced keep "名によって".

source.text: πῶς δύνασθε ὑμεῖς πιστεῦσαι, δόξαν παρ’ ἀλλήλων λαμβάνοντες, καὶ τὴν δόξαν τὴν παρὰ τοῦ μόνου θεοῦ οὐ ζητεῖτε;

records.literal_gloss: How are able you to believe, glory from one another receiving, and the glory the [one] from the only God not you seek?

en.L: How are you able to believe, receiving glory from one another, and the glory that [comes] from the only God you do not seek?
en.B: How could you believe? You accept glory from one another, while the glory that comes from the only God is something you do not seek.
en.R: You accept glory from each other, but you do not look for the glory that comes from the only God. So how can you believe?

es.L: ¿Cómo {{plural_you:pueden ustedes|podéis vosotros}} creer, recibiendo gloria unos de otros, y la gloria que [viene] del único Dios no {{plural_you:buscan|buscáis}}?
es.B: ¿Cómo {{plural_you:podrían|podríais}} creer? {{plural_you:Aceptan|Aceptáis}} gloria unos de otros, mientras que la gloria que viene del único Dios no la {{plural_you:buscan|buscáis}}.
es.R: {{plural_you:Ustedes aceptan|Vosotros aceptáis}} gloria unos de otros, pero no {{plural_you:buscan|buscáis}} la gloria que viene del único Dios. Entonces, ¿cómo {{plural_you:pueden|podéis}} creer?

fr.L: Comment pouvez-vous croire, vous qui recevez de la gloire les uns des autres, et la gloire qui [vient] du Dieu unique, vous ne la cherchez pas ?
fr.B: Comment pourriez-vous croire ? Vous acceptez la gloire que vous vous donnez les uns aux autres, et la gloire qui vient du Dieu unique, vous ne la cherchez pas.
fr.R: Vous acceptez la gloire que vous vous donnez les uns aux autres, mais vous ne cherchez pas la gloire qui vient du Dieu unique. Alors comment pouvez-vous croire ?

sw.L: Ninyi mnawezaje kuamini, mkipokea utukufu kutoka kwa mtu na mwenzake, nao utukufu ulio kutoka kwa Mungu pekee hamuutafuti?
sw.B: Mnawezaje kuamini? Mnapokea utukufu kutoka kwa kila mmoja wenu, lakini utukufu unaotoka kwa Mungu pekee hamuutafuti.
sw.R: Mnapokea utukufu kutoka kwa kila mmoja wenu, lakini hamuutafuti utukufu unaotoka kwa Mungu pekee. Basi mnawezaje kuamini?

vi.L: Làm sao các người có thể tin được, khi các người nhận vinh quang từ nhau, mà vinh quang [đến] từ Đức Chúa Trời duy nhất thì các người không tìm kiếm?
vi.B: Làm sao các người tin được? Các người nhận vinh quang từ nhau, còn vinh quang đến từ Đức Chúa Trời duy nhất thì các người chẳng tìm kiếm.
vi.R: Các người nhận vinh quang từ nhau, nhưng không tìm kiếm vinh quang đến từ Đức Chúa Trời duy nhất. Vậy làm sao các người có thể tin được?

ko.L: 너희가 어떻게 믿을 수 있겠느냐? 서로에게서 영광을 받으면서, 오직 한 분이신 하나님께로부터 오는 영광은 구하지 않으니.
ko.B: 너희가 어떻게 믿을 수 있겠느냐? 너희는 서로에게서 영광을 받으면서도, 오직 한 분이신 하나님께서 주시는 영광은 구하지 않는다.
ko.R: 너희는 서로 칭찬하며 영광을 주고받으면서, 오직 한 분이신 하나님께서 주시는 영광은 찾지 않는다. 그러니 너희가 어떻게 믿을 수 있겠느냐?

pt.L: Como vocês podem crer, recebendo glória uns dos outros, e a glória que [vem] do único Deus vocês não buscam?
pt.B: Como vocês poderiam crer? Vocês aceitam glória uns dos outros, enquanto não buscam a glória que vem do único Deus.
pt.R: Vocês aceitam glória uns dos outros, mas não procuram a glória que vem do único Deus. Então, como vocês podem acreditar?

am.L: እርስ በርሳችሁ ክብርን እየተቀባበላችሁ፣ ብቻውን አምላክ ከሆነው ከእግዚአብሔር የሚገኘውንም ክብር ሳትፈልጉ እንዴት ልታምኑ ትችላላችሁ?
am.B: እንዴት ልታምኑ ትችላላችሁ? እርስ በርሳችሁ ክብር ትቀባበላላችሁ፤ ብቻውን አምላክ ከሆነው ከእግዚአብሔር የሚመጣውን ክብር ግን አትፈልጉም።
am.R: እርስ በርሳችሁ ክብር ትቀባበላላችሁ፤ ብቻውን አምላክ ከሆነው ከእግዚአብሔር የሚመጣውን ክብር ግን አትፈልጉም። ታዲያ እንዴት ልታምኑ ትችላላችሁ?

hi.L: तुम कैसे विश्वास कर सकते हो, जो एक दूसरे से महिमा लेते हो, और वह महिमा जो एकमात्र परमेश्वर से [आती] है, नहीं ढूँढ़ते?
hi.B: तुम विश्वास कैसे कर सकते हो? तुम एक-दूसरे से महिमा स्वीकार करते हो, पर जो महिमा एकमात्र परमेश्वर से आती है, उसे तुम नहीं ढूँढ़ते।
hi.R: तुम एक-दूसरे से महिमा लेते हो, पर उस महिमा की खोज नहीं करते जो एकमात्र परमेश्वर से आती है। तो तुम विश्वास कैसे कर सकते हो?

ru.L: Как можете вы уверовать, принимая славу друг от друга, тогда как славы от единственного Бога не ищете?
ru.B: Как вы могли бы поверить? Вы принимаете славу друг от друга, а славы, что исходит от единственного Бога, не ищете.
ru.R: Вы принимаете славу друг от друга, но не ищете славы, которая приходит от единственного Бога. Как же вы можете поверить?

uk.L: Як ви можете вірити, приймаючи славу один від одного, а слави, що від єдиного Бога, не шукаєте?
uk.B: Як ви могли б повірити? Ви приймаєте славу один від одного, а слави, яка походить від єдиного Бога, не шукаєте.
uk.R: Ви приймаєте славу один від одного, але не шукаєте слави, яка приходить від єдиного Бога. Як же ви можете вірити?

ja.L: 互いに栄光を受け合い、唯一の神からの栄光を求めないあなたがたが、どうして信じることができるだろうか？
ja.B: どうして、あなたがたは信じることができるだろうか？互いに栄光を受け合いながら、唯一の神からの栄光は求めようとしないのだから。
ja.R: あなたたちは、お互いから栄光を受けているのに、ただ一人の神からの栄光を求めようとしない。それで、どうして信じることができるだろうか？

decisions.choice: receiving glory: the reason they cannot believe
alternatives: only a description alongside the question
decisions.reason: The participle gives the cause: people who live for one another's approval cannot accept the one God sent, whom others reject (compare 12:42-43).
The same sense as in 5:41: the honor they give one another against the honor that comes from God.

alternatives: from the only one (some early manuscripts)
decisions.reason: Some early manuscripts, among them the papyri P66 and P75 and Codex Vaticanus, lack the word for God and read "the glory from the only one"; the sense is the same, since the only one is God. The word may have dropped out because, written in the usual short form, it looked very like the ending of the word before it. A reviewer should check this note against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: the only God: the confession that God is one
decisions.reason: Israel confessed that the LORD is one (Deuteronomy 6:4), and Jesus calls the Father "the only true God" (17:3). His hearers honor the one God in word, yet they seek honor from one another.

decisions.choice: How could you believe? You accept ...
alternatives: How can you believe, when you accept ...?
decisions.reason: Balanced asks the question first and then gives the reason as a statement, which keeps the long sentence clear.

decisions.choice: the reason first, then the question
decisions.reason: Readable states what they do and then asks the question, which is easier to follow.
As in English: keeps the long sentence clear.
"Du seul Dieu" could be read as "from God alone"; "du Dieu unique" says plainly that God is one, the confession the words echo (meaning decision m4).

decisions.choice: the question first, then the participle as a trailing clause ending in "-으니"
alternatives: one sentence with the participle before the verb
decisions.reason: Korean puts dependent clauses before the main verb; to keep the Greek's sequence (question, then reason), Literal ends with an elliptical "-으니" clause.

decisions.choice: ብቻውን አምላክ ከሆነው ከእግዚአብሔር (from God, who alone is God)
decisions.reason: The phrase echoes the confession that God is one (meaning decision m4). Amharic says 'the only God' most clearly with "አምላክ" as the predicate, as the style guide sets for that word, and "እግዚአብሔር" as the name.

decisions.choice: the question word "どうして" at the end of one long clause (L)
decisions.reason: Japanese puts the participles describing "you" before the verb, so Literal gathers them into one clause before "どうして信じることができるだろうか"; Balanced asks first and gives the reason after, and Readable gives the reason first, as the English levels do.

decisions.choice: "唯一の神" (L, B); "ただ一人の神" (R)
decisions.reason: The confession that God is one (meaning decision m4); Readable uses plainer words.

source.text: μὴ δοκεῖτε ὅτι ἐγὼ κατηγορήσω ὑμῶν πρὸς τὸν πατέρα· ἔστιν ὁ κατηγορῶν ὑμῶν Μωϋσῆς, εἰς ὃν ὑμεῖς ἠλπίκατε.

records.literal_gloss: Do not think that I will accuse you before the Father; there is the [one] accusing you, Moses, in whom you have hoped.

en.L: Do not think that I will accuse you before the Father; the one who accuses you is Moses, in whom you have hoped.
en.B: Do not imagine that I will be the one to accuse you before the Father. You already have an accuser: Moses, in whom you have put your hope.
en.R: Do not think that I am the one who will accuse you to the Father. Moses is the one who accuses you, the very Moses you have put your hope in.

es.L: No {{plural_you:piensen|penséis}} que yo {{plural_you:los|os}} acusaré ante el Padre; el que {{plural_you:los|os}} acusa es Moisés, en quien {{plural_you:han puesto su esperanza|habéis puesto vuestra esperanza}}.
es.B: No {{plural_you:se imaginen|os imaginéis}} que seré yo quien {{plural_you:los|os}} acuse ante el Padre. Ya {{plural_you:tienen|tenéis}} quien {{plural_you:los|os}} acuse: Moisés, en quien {{plural_you:han puesto su esperanza|habéis puesto vuestra esperanza}}.
es.R: No {{plural_you:piensen|penséis}} que yo soy el que {{plural_you:los|os}} va a acusar ante el Padre. Moisés es el que {{plural_you:los|os}} acusa, el mismo Moisés en quien {{plural_you:han puesto su esperanza|habéis puesto vuestra esperanza}}.

fr.L: Ne pensez pas que {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}}, je vous accuserai devant le Père ; celui qui vous accuse, c’est Moïse, en qui vous avez espéré.
fr.B: N’allez pas imaginer que c’est {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}} qui vous accuserai devant le Père. Vous avez déjà un accusateur : Moïse, en qui vous avez placé votre espérance.
fr.R: Ne pensez pas que c’est {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}} qui vais vous accuser devant le Père. C’est Moïse qui vous accuse, ce Moïse en qui vous avez mis votre espoir.

sw.L: Msifikiri kwamba {{deity_pronoun:mimi|Mimi}} nitawashtaki kwa Baba; mshtaki wenu ni Musa, yule ambaye mmeweka tumaini lenu kwake.
sw.B: Msidhani kwamba {{deity_pronoun:mimi|Mimi}} ndiye nitakayewashtaki mbele ya Baba. Tayari mnaye mshtaki: Musa, mliyemwekea tumaini lenu.
sw.R: Msifikiri kwamba {{deity_pronoun:mimi|Mimi}} ndiye nitakayewashtaki kwa Baba. Musa ndiye anayewashtaki, yule yule Musa mliyemtumainia.

vi.L: Đừng nghĩ rằng {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} sẽ tố cáo các người trước mặt Cha; người tố cáo các người là Môi-se, người mà các người đã trông cậy.
vi.B: Đừng tưởng rằng chính {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} sẽ là người tố cáo các người trước mặt Cha. Các người đã có người tố cáo rồi: đó là Môi-se, người mà các người đặt hy vọng vào.
vi.R: Đừng nghĩ rằng {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} là người sẽ tố cáo các người với Cha. Môi-se mới là người tố cáo các người, chính Môi-se mà các người đặt hy vọng vào.

ko.L: 내가 아버지 앞에서 너희를 고발할 것이라고 생각하지 마라. 너희를 고발하는 이가 있으니, 너희가 소망을 두어 온 모세이다.
ko.B: 내가 아버지 앞에서 너희를 고발하는 사람이 될 것이라고 생각하지 마라. 너희를 고발하는 이는 이미 있다. 바로 너희가 소망을 걸어 온 모세다.
ko.R: 내가 아버지께 너희를 고발할 것이라고 생각하지 마라. 너희를 고발하는 사람은 모세다. 너희가 희망을 걸어 온 바로 그 모세다.

pt.L: Não pensem que eu vou acusá-los diante do Pai; o que os acusa é Moisés, em quem vocês têm esperado.
pt.B: Não imaginem que serei eu quem vai acusá-los diante do Pai. Vocês já têm quem os acuse: Moisés, em quem puseram a esperança.
pt.R: Não pensem que eu sou quem vai acusar vocês diante do Pai. Quem acusa vocês é Moisés, esse mesmo Moisés em quem vocês puseram a esperança.

am.L: በአብ ፊት የምከሳችሁ እኔ እንደ ሆንኩ አታስቡ፤ የሚከሳችሁ ተስፋ ያደረጋችሁበት ሙሴ ነው።
am.B: በአብ ፊት የምከሳችሁ እኔ እሆናለሁ ብላችሁ አታስቡ። ቀድሞውኑ የሚከሳችሁ አለ፤ እርሱም ተስፋ የጣላችሁበት ሙሴ ነው።
am.R: በአብ ፊት የምከሳችሁ እኔ የሆንኩ አይምሰላችሁ። የሚከሳችሁ ሙሴ ነው፤ ተስፋ ያደረጋችሁበት ያው ሙሴ።

hi.L: यह मत सोचो कि मैं पिता के सामने तुम पर दोष लगाऊँगा; तुम पर दोष लगानेवाला तो मूसा है, जिस पर तुमने आशा रखी है।
hi.B: यह मत समझो कि पिता के सामने तुम पर दोष लगानेवाला मैं होऊँगा। तुम पर दोष लगानेवाला तो पहले से है: मूसा, जिस पर तुमने अपनी आशा लगा रखी है।
hi.R: यह मत सोचो कि पिता के सामने तुम पर दोष लगानेवाला मैं हूँ। तुम पर दोष लगानेवाला मूसा है, वही मूसा जिस पर तुमने अपनी आशा लगाई है।

ru.L: Не думайте, что {{deity_pronoun:я|Я}} буду обвинять вас перед Отцом; есть обвиняющий вас — Моисей, на которого вы возложили надежду.
ru.B: Не воображайте, что это {{deity_pronoun:я|Я}} буду обвинять вас перед Отцом. У вас уже есть обвинитель — Моисей, на которого вы возложили свою надежду.
ru.R: Не думайте, что это {{deity_pronoun:я|Я}} буду жаловаться на вас Отцу. Вас обвиняет Моисей — тот самый Моисей, на которого вы надеетесь.

uk.L: Не думайте, що {{deity_pronoun:я|Я}} обвинувачуватиму вас перед Отцем; є той, хто вас обвинувачує, — Мойсей, на якого ви поклали надію.
uk.B: Не уявляйте, що це {{deity_pronoun:я|Я}} обвинувачуватиму вас перед Отцем. У вас уже є обвинувач — Мойсей, на якого ви поклали свою надію.
uk.R: Не думайте, що це {{deity_pronoun:я|Я}} буду обвинувачувати вас перед Отцем. Той, хто вас обвинувачує, — Мойсей, той самий Мойсей, на якого ви надієтеся.

ja.L: わたしが父の前であなたがたを訴えるだろうと思ってはならない。あなたがたを訴えるのは、あなたがたが望みをかけてきたモーセである。
ja.B: わたしが父の前であなたがたを訴えるのだと思ってはならない。あなたがたには、すでに訴える者がいる。あなたがたが望みをかけているモーセである。
ja.R: わたしが父にあなたたちのことを訴えるのだ、と思ってはいけない。あなたたちを訴えるのはモーセだ。あなたたちが頼りにしている、そのモーセなのだ。

decisions.choice: Moses accuses them through the Law he wrote
decisions.reason: Moses was remembered as the one who pleaded with God for Israel (Exodus 32:11-14, 30-32); here he is their accuser instead. Moses himself had the book of the Law placed beside the ark as a witness against the people (Deuteronomy 31:26): the Law they rely on testifies against those who do not listen to it.

decisions.choice: set your hope on Moses: relied on Moses and his Law for their standing with God
decisions.reason: They counted on being disciples of Moses (9:28-29) and keepers of his Law. The perfect tense describes a hope they have held and still hold.

decisions.choice: I: emphatic; it is not Jesus who will bring the charge
decisions.reason: The Father has given all judgment to the Son (5:22, 27), yet Jesus says he will not need to accuse them; the pronoun stresses the contrast with Moses. Elsewhere he says he came not to judge the world but to save it (3:17; 12:47-48).
The present participle "the one accusing" describes an accuser already at work; Balanced says so.
The perfect tense describes a settled hope; "put your hope in" says that more naturally than "have hoped".

decisions.choice: I will be the one to accuse (B); I am the one who will accuse (R)
decisions.reason: Shows the emphatic pronoun (meaning decision m3).

decisions.choice: seré yo quien (B); yo soy el que (R)
decisions.reason: Shows the emphatic pronoun (meaning decision m3).
As in English: an accuser already at work.
"고발하다" is the plain modern word for bringing a charge; "송사하다" is old church language.

source.text: εἰ γὰρ ἐπιστεύετε Μωϋσεῖ, ἐπιστεύετε ἂν ἐμοί, περὶ γὰρ ἐμοῦ ἐκεῖνος ἔγραψεν.

records.literal_gloss: For if you were believing Moses, you would believe me; for about me that one wrote.

en.L: For if you believed Moses, you would believe {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}; for it was about {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} that he wrote.

decisions.choice: a condition contrary to fact: they do not really believe Moses
decisions.reason: The form of the sentence assumes the opposite of the if-clause: they do not believe Moses, and so they do not believe Jesus. Their hope in Moses (5:45) is not real belief in what he wrote.

decisions.choice: the writings of Moses as a whole point to Jesus
alternatives: one particular passage, such as the promise of a prophet like Moses (Deuteronomy 18:15-18)
decisions.reason: Jesus does not name a passage. The books of Moses, Genesis to Deuteronomy, contain promises and patterns that John elsewhere connects with Jesus: Philip speaks of the one Moses wrote about in the Law (1:45); the crowds wonder whether Jesus is the Prophet (6:14; 7:40), the prophet like Moses whom God promised to raise up (Deuteronomy 18:15-18); and Jesus compares himself to the serpent Moses lifted up (3:14) and to the manna (6:31-35).

decisions.choice: believe someone: take that person's word as true
decisions.reason: With a person as its object in this form, the verb means to believe what the person says, not yet to "believe in" him. Jesus asks his hearers to trust his words as they claim to trust Moses's (5:47).
Shows that the condition is contrary to fact (meaning decision m1).
As in English: shows that the condition is contrary to fact (meaning decision m1). "Creer a" + person, not "creer en" (m3); "él" is Moses.
Vietnamese marks a condition contrary to fact (meaning decision) with "hẳn đã": you would have believed, but you do not. A plain "sẽ tin" would read as a promise.

decisions.choice: crer em Moisés ... crer em mim
decisions.reason: The English can say "believe Moses" without "in" (meaning decision m3). In Portuguese "crer em" / "acreditar em" a person is also the ordinary way to say that one takes their word as true, so it is used here as in 5:24.
